_comment: Editable rules consumed by scripts/build_fueleu_group_map.py. Patterns are JS/Python-regex source strings matched case-insensitively against MRV parent_name. thirdPartyManagerPatterns are checked first (after manualOverrides), then ownerBrandPatterns, in array order (first match wins). manualOverrides key on company_imo and are for subsidiary/brand relationships that are NOT obvious from the entity name itself, so each one carries a sourceUrl.

ownerBrandPatterns.group_name: Capital Ship Management / Capital Product Partners

1250463.note: Finnlines Plc has been a subsidiary of the Grimaldi Group since Grimaldi's 2006-2008 acquisition of a controlling stake.

5022388.note: Finnlines Ship Management AB is the crewing/technical-management subsidiary of Finnlines Plc, itself Grimaldi Group-controlled.

0080148.note: Grimaldi's Compagnia di Navigazione S.p.A. has owned/controlled 95.9% of Minoan Lines since 2008.

0254141.note: Moby SpA is the lead operating company of the Onorato family's Moby Group (MSC/Aponte family's 49% stake is being handed back after the AGCM commitments of 24 Oct 2025).

5575771.note: Wilhelmsen Lines Shipowning Malta Limited is a legacy Wilhelmsen-side shipowning entity operating within the Wallenius Wilhelmsen network formed by the 1999 Wallenius/Wilhelmsen tie-up.

6462013.group_name: Wisdom Synergy Ship Management Pte Ltd
6462013.note: Name contains 'Synergy' and would otherwise match the Synergy Marine Group third-party-manager pattern, but no evidence was found that Wisdom Synergy Ship Management Pte Ltd is part of, or affiliated with, Synergy Marine Group -- kept as its own single-company placeholder group instead of merged.

groupParents._comment: Optional group_id -> parent_group_id links for corporate parent/subsidiary group relationships (distinct from manualOverrides, which reassigns a COMPANY to a group; this instead links two already-formed GROUPS). Applied after all groups are built.

msc-cruises.note: MSC Cruises is part of the MSC Group (Aponte family) alongside MSC's container-shipping arm.

segmentFuelCostBearer._basis: Under a time charter the charterer normally pays for and supplies bunkers (owner pays only under a bareboat/voyage charter or when self-operating). BIMCO's FuelEU Maritime Clause for Time Charter Parties 2024 formalises this by passing FuelEU compliance balances/costs and compliance-strategy choices (pooling, banking, borrowing) to the time charterer. These are INDUSTRY-TYPICAL defaults per trade/segment, not a fact about any specific company -- many vessels in the 'owner-operator' segments are still time-chartered out, and vice versa.

Container ship.note: Liner container shipping is dominated by vertically integrated carriers (Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, COSCO, Hapag-Lloyd, ONE, Evergreen, HMM, ZIM, Yang Ming) that own/control tonnage and bunker purchasing directly; typical.

Container/ro-ro cargo ship.note: ConRo tonnage is generally deployed on owner-operated liner-type services (e.g. Grimaldi, ACL); typical.

Ro-pax ship.note: Ferry/ro-pax operators (DFDS, Stena, Grimaldi, Attica Group, Tallink, etc.) typically own and directly operate their tonnage on fixed routes; typical.

Ro-ro ship.note: Pure ro-ro tonnage spans owner-operated short-sea services and vessels time-chartered into car-carrier/forest-product pools; no single typical bearer.

Passenger ship.note: Cruise and coastal-passenger operators (Carnival, RCG, NCLH, MSC Cruises, TUI Cruises, Hurtigruten, etc.) own/control their vessels directly; typical.

Passenger ship (Cruise Passenger ship).note: As with Passenger ship: cruise brands are vertically integrated owner-operators; typical.

Bulk carrier.note: Dry bulk is a tramp trade dominated by time/voyage chartering; under BIMCO's FuelEU Time Charter Clause the time charterer, who supplies bunkers, bears FuelEU compliance cost/strategy choices; typical.

Oil tanker.note: Tanker tonnage is predominantly chartered out (time or voyage) to oil majors/traders who control bunkering; under time charter the charterer bears fuel and FuelEU cost per BIMCO's clause; typical.

Chemical tanker.note: Chemical tankers trade on similar tramp/COA chartering patterns to oil tankers; typical.

Gas carrier.note: LPG/gas carriers below LNG scale are largely time-chartered to gas traders/majors who bunker the vessel; typical.

LNG carrier.note: LNG carriers are usually fixed on long-term time charters to energy majors/traders (who as charterer would bear FuelEU cost under the BIMCO clause), but many run on cargo boil-off gas supplied by the cargo owner, blurring who 'bears' the marine fuel cost; treated as mixed rather than a clean default.

General cargo ship.note: General cargo/multipurpose tonnage trades tramp-style, typically time- or voyage-chartered; typical.

Refrigerated cargo carrier.note: Reefer vessels are typically time-chartered into seasonal fruit/produce trades by charterers who supply bunkers; typical.

Vehicle carrier.note: Pure car/truck carriers (PCTC) split between owner-operators with captive OEM cargo (e.g. Wallenius Wilhelmsen, Eukor, Hoegh, NYK/MOL/K Line car-carrier arms) and tonnage time-chartered to OEMs/trading houses; no single typical bearer.

Combination carrier.note: Combination/OBO carriers are a small, heterogeneous segment trading across both bulk and tanker charter markets; no single typical bearer.

Other ship types.note: Catch-all MRV category covering heterogeneous vessel types with no single typical chartering pattern.

Other ship types (Offshore).note: Offshore support/specialist tonnage is chartered under project- and campaign-specific contracts (often bareboat or specialised time charters) with no single typical FuelEU cost bearer.
